question: Should OpenClaw accept a gateway-owned node-backed ACP runtime in core now, and under what storage, security, and proof gates?
rationale: The PR adds a major runtime, durable state model, and node command trust surface; code review can identify blockers, but maintainers need to decide whether this belongs in core now and what upgrade/security contract it must satisfy.

options.title: Require repair before merge
options.body: Keep the PR open but require SQLite-backed durable state, explicit ACP command security gating, delivery/reconnect/session fixes, and real paired-node proof before merge.

options.title: Sponsor a narrower staged runtime
options.body: Ask for smaller implementation slices after maintainer approval of the ACP node runtime API, storage schema, and trust model.

options.title: Close for design rework
options.body: Close this branch if core ACP node runtime ownership is not accepted yet and revive the work through a design issue or smaller future PRs.

recommendation.title: Require repair before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but require SQLite-backed durable state, explicit ACP command security gating, delivery/reconnect/session fixes, and real paired-node proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across ACP dispatch, gateway node identity, and adjacent runtime ownership surfaces affected by the decision.
